title: Building a Simple Chatbot
description: Let's design a friendly study-helper chatbot and learn how conversational AI really works.

content.value: A chatbot is a program you can talk to. It takes your message, figures out what you mean, and replies. Simple chatbots follow rules ('if the user says hello, reply hi'), while advanced ones like ChatGPT use powerful AI language models.
It helps to know the difference between the two main types, because they work very differently under the hood:

📏  Rule-based chatbot
     Follows a fixed list of 'if this, say that' rules.
     Predictable, but only handles what it was told.
     Example: a pizza-ordering menu bot.

🧠  AI-powered chatbot
     Uses an NLP language model trained on huge text.
     Flexible, can handle questions it never saw before.
     Example: ChatGPT, Claude.

A rule-based bot is like a vending machine: press B4, get exactly the snack in slot B4. An AI-powered bot is more like a helpful librarian who understands your question even if you phrase it in a new way.
Your Project: A Study Buddy Bot
Let's design a chatbot that helps students. It should be able to:

💬  Answer common questions   ('What's the homework?')
💡  Give quiz hints           ('Need a hint? Think about data!')
📚  Share study tips          ('Try the Pomodoro technique!')
A simple chatbot matches what you type to a list of patterns and picks a reply. Here's the basic idea written like a recipe:

IF the message contains 'hello'  → say 'Hi there! 👋'
IF the message contains 'hint'   → give a small clue
IF the message contains 'tip'    → share a study tip
OTHERWISE                         → say 'Can you ask that another way?'
See that last line? The 'otherwise' reply is important. A good chatbot always has a friendly fallback for when it doesn't understand, so the conversation never hits a dead end.

Build it yourself! Free tools like Scratch, MIT App Inventor, and web-based chatbot builders let you create a working chatbot by dragging blocks together, no typing code required. Start with 3 rules and a fallback, then add more.

Key Takeaway: Chatbots are conversational AI systems that understand a message and choose a helpful reply, rule-based ones follow fixed patterns, while AI-powered ones use language models to handle almost anything.

quiz.question: What is a chatbot?
options: A program you can talk to that understands and replies
quiz.explain: A chatbot reads your message, works out what you mean, and responds, that's conversational AI.

quiz.question: How does a simple rule-based chatbot decide what to say?
options: It randomly guesses with no logic
It matches your message to patterns and picks a reply
It calls a human every time
quiz.explain: Rule-based chatbots look for patterns in your message ('if it contains hint...') and respond accordingly.

quiz.question: Which tool can you use to build a chatbot without writing code?
quiz.explain: Block-based tools like Scratch and MIT App Inventor let you build chatbots by dragging blocks together.

quiz.question: What is the main difference between a rule-based bot and an AI-powered bot?
options: A rule-based bot follows fixed rules; an AI-powered bot uses a language model to handle new questions
quiz.explain: Rule-based bots only handle what they were told, while AI-powered bots use NLP models to respond flexibly to questions they've never seen.
